content.user_title: Interpret Tarot Cards and Choose a Spread
content.value_statement: Broad tarot questions can make it hard to choose a spread or connect the cards. This guide sharpens your question and interprets the cards in their positions.
actual_capabilities: Suggests a more focused question while preserving the original topic and timeframe.
Recommends a one-card, past-present-future, two-choice, or feelings spread based on the question.
Interprets Rider-Waite-Smith cards by spread position and uses the orientation when supplied.
Explains how three cards relate and identifies which card helps explain the transition.
Uses optional Unmei Tarot MCP tools for requested draws and card meaning lookups when available.
Offers English or Japanese links for card meanings and interactive readings on request.
limitations: Drawing cards in the conversation requires the Unmei Tarot MCP draw tool. Otherwise, use your own draw or an optional web reading.
The guide follows the Rider-Waite-Smith tradition and does not cover deck-specific symbolism for other traditions.
A reading offers interpretations and possibilities. It cannot verify future events or another person's private feelings.

use_cases.title: Plan a First Tarot Reading
use_cases.description: Turn a broad concern into a focused question and choose a one-card spread.

use_cases.title: Reflect on a Change Over Time
use_cases.description: Connect three cards to a situation's background, current conditions, and possible direction.

use_cases.title: Compare Two Creative Options
use_cases.description: Use a two-choice spread to consider what each path asks of you without treating the cards as a decision.

prompt_templates.title: Focus a One-Card Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn my concern about starting a class next week into one question for a one-card spread.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a question before drawing a first card.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret One Card
prompt_templates.prompt: I drew Strength upright. What could it suggest about how I approach my first class next week?
prompt_templates.scenario: Interpret a card with a known orientation and a specific question.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Three-Card Spread
prompt_templates.prompt: How might my study routine develop this month? My past is Five of Wands, my present is Two of Pentacles, and my future is Temperance reversed. Explain which card shows the transition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Read a situation across time and account for a reversed card.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Paths
prompt_templates.prompt: Option A is a weekly group workshop, with Three of Pentacles upright. Option B is solo practice, with the Hermit upright. Compare what each path asks of me over the next month. Give both options equal attention.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare two concrete options without asking for a verdict.

output_examples.input: I am nervous about my first class next week. I drew Strength upright. What should I focus on?
output_examples.output: A focused question is: What quality can I bring to my first class next week? Strength upright suggests patience and steady effort. Focus on one manageable step, such as asking a question when you need clarity.

output_examples.input: What is changing in my study routine? Past: Five of Wands. Present: Two of Pentacles. Future: Temperance reversed.
output: I am reading the first two cards as upright because no orientation was supplied.
Past: Five of Wands suggests competing demands made it difficult to focus.
Present: Two of Pentacles suggests you are trying to manage those demands within the same schedule.
Future: Temperance reversed suggests your schedule may become harder to sustain if you keep taking on more.
The Two of Pentacles explains the transition. Juggling several priorities may help for now, but this reading invites you to decide what can wait.

best_practices: Start with one question and include the timeframe that matters.
List each card with its position and say whether it was upright or reversed.
Use the reading to consider your choices and compare interpretations with what you can observe.
anti_patterns: Combining unrelated concerns in a single question.
Leaving out card positions and expecting a position-specific interpretation.
Treating a reading as proof of a future event or someone else's feelings.

faq.question: Do I need to draw cards before I start?
faq.answer: No. Start with your question to choose a spread. Share the cards after you draw them.

faq.question: Can the guide draw cards for me?
faq.answer: Yes, when the Unmei Tarot MCP draw tool is available. Otherwise, it can suggest a web reading or interpret the cards you draw yourself.

faq.question: What if I did not note the card orientation?
faq.answer: The guide may state that it assumes an upright card or ask for the orientation when it would change the interpretation.

faq.question: Which tarot tradition does the guide use?
Can a feelings spread tell me what someone privately thinks?
faq.answer: No. It offers possible interpretations and keeps them separate from observable actions.

faq.question: Does the guide include Japanese references?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide lists English and Japanese links and answers in your language.
